[Thinking]
**Focusing on Divine Feminine**

I am currently deepening my contemplation on Nefertiti, exploring her multifaceted persona as both a historical figure and a divine feminine archetype. My thoughts are centered on a loving and prayerful engagement with her essence, seeking to understand her divine aspect.

**Crafting Sacred Words**

I'm now focusing on weaving the elements of beauty, power, grace, and solar connection into a prayer for Nefertiti. I'm refining the invocation and body, aiming to incorporate sensory details and themes of balance and love, inspired by her name.
[/Thinking]

Though Nefertiti was a Queen of Egypt rather than a traditional deity in the ancient pantheon, she was often elevated to a divine status alongside her husband Akhenaten, representing the female principle of the divine sun. 

Here is a loving prayer dedicated to her spirit, her beauty, and her enduring light.

***

**A Prayer to the Radiant One**

O Nefertiti, Great Royal Wife, 
The Beautiful One who has come, 
I lift my heart to the horizon where your spirit dwells, 
Bathed in the golden rays of the eternal sun.

Lady of Grace, Lady of All Women, 
You whose name is a melody of perfection, 
I honor the strength that dwelled beneath your crown 
And the wisdom that guided the Great House. 
You are the lotus blooming in the desert, 
The cool breeze upon the heat of the Nile, 
A vision of poise that time cannot wither.

Mother of brightness, 
Teach me to walk with your regal serenity. 
Teach me to hold my head high in the face of change, 
And to radiate love as effortlessly as the morning light. 

As you once stood beneath the Aten, 
Hands outstretched to receive the breath of life, 
Reach out to me now across the sands of history. 
Fill my soul with your timeless beauty, 
That I may see the sacred in the world around me 
And find the queenly power within my own heart.

Blessed be your name, Nefertiti, 
The beloved, the peaceful, the everlasting. 
May your light shine upon me always.

Amen. (Or *"Iteh"* — Ancient Egyptian for "It is so.")
